original_question: Let G1 and G2 be two connected nonsingular block graphs, and let v1 be a vertex of G1 and v2 be a vertex of G2. If one adds a new edge between v1 and v2 and the resulting graph is still a block graph, must the resulting block graph also be nonsingular?
target_in_paper: Closest match: Proposition 1.2 in Section 1 of the withdrawn paper, i.e. the edge-joining reformulation of Conjecture 1.1, read together with Theorem 1.3 as the nearby positive result. This identification is based on the arXiv record for the withdrawn paper and the closely corresponding edge-joining/tree-of-block-graphs discussion in Section 3 of the later published paper by the same authors. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.03947))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the central operation (joining two already nonsingular block graphs by one new edge), the intended yes/no closure question, and the ambient graph class of connected block graphs. It also uses the paper's singular/nonsingular language at the graph level, rather than switching to a different matrix class or a broader graph family. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.03947))
missing_details: The paper's basic notion of 'nonsingular' is with respect to the (0,1)-adjacency matrix A(G), and the ambient field is the real numbers. That definition should be stated explicitly. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.03947))
The graphs should be specified as finite simple undirected block graphs; otherwise the question is not fully stand-alone. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.03947))

If the formulation uses two graphs G1 and G2 and then adds an edge between v1 and v2, one should say that G1 and G2 are vertex-disjoint (or that disjoint copies are taken first). ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S002437952030238X?utm_source=openai))

The exact quantifiers should be explicit: the question is whether this preservation of nonsingularity holds for every choice of connected nonsingular block graphs and every choice of joining vertices allowed by the formulation. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S002437952030238X?utm_source=openai))

The nearby context suggests that this edge-joining question is meant as a reformulation of a broader conjecture about connected block graphs whose blocks have size at least 3 and contain at least one non-cut-vertex; your draft omits that equivalent broader form. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S002437952030238X?utm_source=openai))

As written, the clause 'and the resulting graph is still a block graph' is not fully clarified. In the later published tree-of-block-graphs construction, the resulting graph is declared to be a block graph by construction, so the intended scope should be stated more sharply rather than left implicit. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S002437952030238X?utm_source=openai))

The arXiv record explicitly says the withdrawn draft's conjectures are wrong, so if you want paper-faithfulness, the refined question should be presented as the paper's conjectural problem, not as an established theorem. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.03947))
refined_question: Let G1 and G2 be finite simple vertex-disjoint connected block graphs, and let v1 ∈ V(G1) and v2 ∈ V(G2). Assume that G1 and G2 are nonsingular, meaning that their (0,1)-adjacency matrices A(G1) and A(G2) are nonsingular over R. If G is obtained from G1 ∪ G2 by adding the single new edge v1v2 (so that G is again a block graph), must G also be nonsingular? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.03947))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, as suggested by the paper's Section 1 reformulation, is every connected block graph G nonsingular whenever every block of G has at least three vertices and contains at least one non-cut-vertex? ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S002437952030238X?utm_source=openai))
justification: The withdrawn arXiv record confirms the paper's topic, terminology, and the fact that its conjectures were later retracted. Because the full withdrawn PDF is not available from the arXiv record, the closest recoverable match must be triangulated from the Section 1 labels named in your instructions and from the later published paper by the same authors, whose Section 3 explicitly develops the same edge-joining/'tree of block graphs' construction (Definition 3.2) and a nearby positive theorem (Theorem 3.7). That context makes your draft look like the edge-joining reformulation in Proposition 1.2 rather than a different later section, while the broader connected-block-graph statement is the natural equivalent formulation to record separately. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.03947))
